parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Procedure for solid K
The student:
• puts some solid K into a clean test-tube
• adds some dilute hydrochloric acid to the test-tube.
Solid K reacts slowly. After ten minutes a pale blue solution is seen in the test-tube.
Suggest two ways the student can make the reaction faster.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Procedure for solid L
The student:
• puts some solid L into a clean test-tube
• adds some dilute hydrochloric acid to the test-tube.
The mixture fizzes and a blue solution is seen in the test-tube.
The gas made in this reaction turns limewater milky.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State the name of the gas made in this reaction.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Circle the negative ion present in L.
carbonate chloride nitrate sulfate

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Procedure for solid M
The student:
• puts some dilute hydrochloric acid into a clean test-tube
• places a thermometer into the dilute hydrochloric acid
• adds a small piece of solid M
• tests the gas made.
All of solid M reacts.
Hydrogen gas is made, and heat energy is released.
The student observes a colourless solution.
Describe three other observations the student makes.
